ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the first quadrant of the xOy coordinate plane, there is a uniform electric field directed along the negative y-axis, and in the fourth quadrant, there is a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane and pointing inward. A particle with mass $m$ and charge $+q$ (neglecting gravity) is injected into the magnetic field from the origin $O$ with an incident direction at a $45^\circ$ angle to the y-axis. When the particle reaches point $P$ with coordinates $(3L, L)$ in the electric field, its velocity has a magnitude of $V_0$ and is directed along the positive x-axis.

1. What is the speed $V$ of the particle when it enters the magnetic field from point O?
2. The magnitude of the electric field strength $E$ in a uniform electric field and the magnetic induction $B$ in a uniform magnetic field?
3. The time taken for the particle to move from point O to point P?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the first quadrant of the coordinate system in the figure, multiple vertically downward arrows are drawn, indicating that the direction of the uniform electric field is along the negative y-axis; in the fourth quadrant, multiple “×” are drawn, indicating that the uniform magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper and directed inward. The particle enters the fourth-quadrant magnetic field from near the origin O in a direction making 45° with the y-axis, then enters the first-quadrant electric field from a certain point A on the x-axis, and finally reaches P(3L,L). In the figure, the velocity at point P is labeled v0, with direction horizontally to the right. According to the problem statement and method, set A=(x_A,0). In the electric field, the particle is subject only to the vertically downward electric-field force, so the horizontal velocity remains unchanged; when reaching P, the velocity is along the +x direction and has magnitude V0, so in the electric field v_x=V0. Let the velocity of the particle just as it enters the electric field be (V0,u), where u is the vertically upward component of velocity. The magnitude of the electric-field acceleration is a=qE/m, with direction downward. When reaching P, the vertical velocity decreases to 0, and the vertical displacement is L, therefore L=u^2/(2a). The time of motion in the electric field is t_E=u/a, and the horizontal displacement satisfies 3L-x_A=V0 t_E=V0 u/a. In the magnetic field, the Lorentz force does no work, and the particle speed remains the speed V when entering the magnetic field. According to the given geometric method, the tangent of the particle at O is 45° downward, and the tangent when it leaves the magnetic field at A and enters the electric field is 45° upward; the circular arc corresponds to a quarter circle. Since the tangent at A makes 45° with the x-axis, there is u=V0. Substituting into the vertical motion formula L=u^2/(2a), obtain a=V0^2/(2L), so E=ma/q=mV0^2/(2qL). In the electric field, t_E=u/a=V0/(V0^2/(2L))=2L/V0. The horizontal displacement is V0 t_E=2L, therefore 3L-x_A=2L, obtaining x_A=L. The endpoints O and A of the magnetic-field circular arc are both on the x-axis, and the chord length OA=L; a quarter circle corresponds to chord length R√2, so R=L/√2. The velocity components of the particle at A are (V0,V0), so the speed in the magnetic field is V=√(V0^2+V0^2)=√2 V0. From qVB=mV^2/R, obtain B=mV/(qR)=m√2V0/[q(L/√2)]=2mV0/(qL). The arc length in the magnetic field is (π/2)R, so t_B=[(π/2)R]/V=π(L/√2)/(2√2V0)=πL/(4V0). The total time t=t_E+t_B=2L/V0+πL/(4V0)=(8+π)L/(4V0).
